skill.name: analyzing-test-quality
skill.description: Analyzes framework-agnostic test quality, coverage signals, reliability risks, maintainability issues, and mutation testing opportunities for software projects.
skill.summary: Audits test suites for reliability, maintainability, coverage quality, and improvement priorities.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: All static alerts were adjudicated as false positives. The Bash helper performs read-only local metrics collection with hardcoded commands, and the SKILL.md backticks are Markdown examples. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, credential access, or destructive file operation was found.

remediation.issue: The Bash metrics script scans the current working tree.
remediation.suggestion: Document that it reads local test and source files only, and advise users to run it in trusted repositories.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes optional npm and npx examples for mutation testing.
remediation.suggestion: State that package installation and mutation tool commands require explicit user confirmation before execution.

content.value_statement: Weak tests hide defects, slow refactoring, and make coverage numbers misleading. This skill analyzes test suites and gives prioritized guidance for reliability, maintainability, coverage, and mutation testing.
actual_capabilities: Assess test quality across correctness, readability, maintainability, reliability, speed, and coverage.
Use a checklist to identify flaky tests, test pollution, over-mocking, and weak assertions.
Explain coverage metrics and show why high coverage may still miss defects.
Guide mutation testing setup and interpretation with Stryker examples.
Provide a reusable report format for prioritizing test suite improvements.
limitations: It does not provide deep framework-specific syntax for Jest, Vitest, Playwright, or Mocha.
Metrics from the shell helper are heuristic and depend on common file naming patterns.
It cannot prove test effectiveness without executing the project test suite.
Mutation testing guidance requires project setup and package manager access.

use_cases.title: Audit Release Readiness
use_cases.description: Review test quality before a release and prioritize defects in the test suite.

use_cases.title: Find Reliability Risks
use_cases.description: Identify flaky patterns, shared state, weak async handling, and missing edge-case coverage.

use_cases.title: Improve Existing Tests
use_cases.description: Refactor brittle tests for readability and maintainability without changing product behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review Test Quality
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner audit of an existing test suite.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the tests in this repository for readability, reliability, coverage gaps, and common anti-patterns. Give prioritized recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret Coverage Results
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review after generating coverage data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this coverage summary and explain the highest-value missing tests. Separate critical path gaps from low-value coverage work.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Mutation Testing
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced setup for measuring assertion strength.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me introduce mutation testing for this project. Recommend configuration, thresholds, and how to interpret surviving mutants.

prompt_templates.title: Create Improvement Roadmap
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a team test quality initiative.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the test suite using the quality checklist and report template. Produce a phased plan with risks, metrics, and owner-ready tasks.

output_examples.input: Review a test suite with many asynchronous UI tests and intermittent failures.
output_examples.output: The report highlights timing dependencies, missing wait conditions, and shared state. It recommends replacing fixed delays and isolating setup.

output_examples.input: Interpret 90 percent line coverage with weak branch coverage.
output_examples.output: The analysis explains why the suite may miss decision paths. It prioritizes boundary tests, error paths, and integration points.

output_examples.input: Evaluate whether mutation testing is worth adding.
output_examples.output: The guidance compares cost, runtime, and expected value. It suggests starting with core business logic before setting thresholds.

best_practices: Run the metrics helper from the repository root and review results with human judgment.
Pair coverage data with code review, mutation results, and failure history.
Prioritize deterministic, readable tests before increasing test volume.
anti_patterns: Treating coverage percentage as the only quality signal.
Running package installation or mutation tools without user confirmation.
Applying framework-specific recommendations when a specialized testing skill is available.

faq.question: Does this skill run my tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can suggest commands and interpret results, but tool execution depends on user approval and the active environment.

faq.question: Can it analyze Jest or Playwright projects?
faq.answer: Yes, for framework-agnostic quality issues. Use a framework-specific skill for detailed syntax and runner patterns.

faq.question: What does the metrics script do?
faq.answer: It counts local test files, source files, test blocks, and common patterns using shell tools.

faq.question: Does it send code outside my machine?
faq.answer: No. The included helper uses local shell commands and no network requests.

faq.question: Can it replace a human test review?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured findings and priorities, but project context still matters.

faq.question: When should I use mutation testing?
faq.answer: Use it for important logic where ordinary coverage does not show whether assertions catch real defects.
